title: Find the doers
instructions: Tap the five doers: the person or thing that does each action.
text: The goalkeeper caught the ball. Then a gust of wind knocked over the scoreboard. Our coach blew her whistle, and the fans cheered. The referee checked his watch.
explanation: The goalkeeper caught · the wind knocked over · our coach blew · the fans cheered · the referee checked. In every sentence the doer comes first, before the verb: that’s the active voice.

title: Active or passive?
instructions: Does the sentence start with the doer (active) or with the thing that receives the action (passive)?

items.text: Maya kicked the ball.
The ball was kicked by Maya.
My bike was stolen last night.
The chef made a giant pancake.
The anthem is sung before every game.
The storm flooded the basement.
The winners will be announced on Friday.
The kids built a fort out of blankets.
The letter was written by my great-grandmother.
Our puppy chewed my homework.

questions.prompt: In “The window was broken by Leo,” who did the breaking?
questions.explanation: “By Leo” names the doer. The window is the receiver: it had the action done to it.

questions.prompt: In “The cookies were eaten,” who ate the cookies?
questions.explanation: A passive sentence doesn’t have to name the doer. Here we only know what happened to the cookies.

questions.prompt: What is the receiver in “The coach praised the team”?
questions.explanation: The coach does the praising; the team receives it. The doer comes first, so this sentence is active.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The bees chased Omar across the field.
Omar was chased across the field by the bees.

questions.explanation: “Was chased” is a form of be + a past participle, and the receiver (Omar) comes first.

questions.prompt: Which two words are a clue that a sentence might be passive?

options.text: a form of be (is, was, were…) + a past participle (taken, built…)

questions.explanation: The passive is built from be + a past participle: is made, was taken, were built. Often “by” + the doer comes next.

title: Doer first, receiver first
prompt: Write four sentences about something that happened at school or at home this week (a spill, a game, a lost item, a surprise). Each sentence has its own task, listed above the writing box. Write them in order.
tips: Active: doer + verb + receiver. “My sister spilled the paint.”
Passive: receiver + be + past participle (+ by the doer). “The paint was spilled by my sister.”
When you don’t know who did it, leave out “by”: “My pencil case was taken.”

sentences.ask: Say what someone did, with the doer first (active).
Tell the same thing with the receiver first, and “by” + the doer at the end (passive).
Say what happened to something when nobody knows who did it (passive, no “by”).
Finish with an active sentence and a strong action verb.

title: Doer to the front
instructions: Rewrite each passive sentence in the active voice. Move the doer (after “by”) to the front and keep the same tense.

items.source: The ball was kicked by Maya.
items.explanation: Doer (Maya) + verb (kicked) + receiver (the ball). “Was kicked” in the past → “kicked”.

items.source: The cookies were eaten by my little brother.
answers: My little brother ate the cookies.
hints: “Were eaten” in the active past is “ate”.
items.explanation: My little brother (doer) ate (past) the cookies (receiver).

items.source: The mural was painted by the art club.
answers: The art club painted the mural.
items.explanation: The doer moves to the front, and the passive “was painted” becomes the active “painted”.

items.task: Make it active. (It’s in the present tense.)
items.source: The windows are cleaned by Mr. Patel every Friday.
answers: Mr. Patel cleans the windows every Friday.
Every Friday, Mr. Patel cleans the windows.
Every Friday Mr. Patel cleans the windows.
items.explanation: “Are cleaned” is present, so the active verb is present too: Mr. Patel cleans.

items.task: Make it active. (It’s in the future.)
items.source: The dog will be walked by Grandpa.
items.explanation: “Will be walked” (future passive) → “will walk” (future active).

items.source: The old oak tree was knocked down by the storm.
answers: The storm knocked down the old oak tree.
The storm knocked the old oak tree down.
items.explanation: The doer doesn’t have to be a person: the storm is doing the action.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is clearer and stronger?

options.text: A home run was hit by Ana in the last inning.
Ana hit a home run in the last inning.

questions.explanation: The active sentence puts Ana first and uses fewer words. Readers see who acted straight away.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the active voice?

options.text: The test was graded by Ms. Ruiz.

questions.explanation: In “Ms. Ruiz graded the test,” the doer (Ms. Ruiz) comes before the verb.

questions.prompt: Count the words: “The song was sung by the choir” (7) vs “The choir sang the song.” How many words does the active save?
questions.explanation: The active version has 5 words. Dropping “was” and “by” makes it tighter.

questions.prompt: Is “Sam is running to the bus” active or passive?
questions.explanation: “Is running” is be + an -ing verb (progressive), not be + a past participle. Sam does the running, so it’s active.

questions.prompt: Why do essay writers mostly use the active voice?

options.text: It shows clearly who does what, in fewer words.

questions.explanation: The passive isn’t wrong, but the active is usually more direct. Use the passive on purpose (that’s Lesson 5).

title: Pick the active verb
instructions: Choose the verb that keeps the sentence in the active voice, with the doer first.

items.sentence: The chef ___ the soup with fresh basil.
items.explanation: The chef does the topping: “The chef topped the soup.”

items.sentence: The wind ___ the kite into the clouds.
items.explanation: The wind is the doer, so it gets the active verb: lifted.

items.sentence: Our class ___ two hundred cans for the food drive.
items.explanation: Our class did the collecting: active.

items.sentence: Tomorrow, the judges ___ the best robot.
items.explanation: The judges do the choosing. “Will be chosen” would make the judges the ones being picked!

items.sentence: Firefighters ___ the cat from the roof.
items.explanation: Firefighters rescued the cat. (“Were rescued” would mean someone rescued the firefighters.)
Grandma did the sewing: “My grandma sewed this quilt.”

title: Sports desk
prompt: You’re a sports reporter. Write a short news report (6–10 sentences) about a game, a race or a match (real or made up). Use the active voice in every sentence: put the player or team first, then a strong action verb.
tips: Doer + strong verb: “Jordan sprinted down the sideline.” “The Hawks crushed the Tigers 4–1.”
Spot a “was … by”? Flip it: “The goal was scored by Lee” → “Lee scored the goal.”
Strong verbs: sprinted, blocked, smashed, dodged, snatched, rallied, sealed.

title: Build the passive
instructions: Choose the passive verb that fits the tense. The time words are your clue.

items.sentence: Fresh bread ___ every morning at the corner bakery.
items.hint: “Every morning” means it happens again and again: the present.
items.explanation: Present passive: am/is/are + past participle → is baked.

items.hint: 1889 is a finished time in the past.
items.explanation: Past passive: was/were + past participle → was completed.
Future passive: will be + past participle → will be opened.

items.sentence: Shh! The baby’s room ___ right now.
items.explanation: Present progressive passive: is/are being + past participle → is being painted.

items.sentence: Good news: all the tickets ___ already.
items.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle → have been sold.

items.sentence: Last year, the school’s old computers ___ to a charity.
items.hint: Computers: more than one. And “gave” isn’t a participle.
items.explanation: Plural subject → were; give → given. The passive always needs the past participle.

items.sentence: When we arrived, the stage ___ by the crew.
items.hint: It was in progress when we arrived (in the past).
items.explanation: Past progressive passive: was/were being + past participle → was being set up.

items.sentence: The answer ___ on the back of the card.
items.hint: write, wrote, … which form goes after be?
items.explanation: The past participle of write is written: is written.

title: Passive tense sort
instructions: Every sentence is passive. Which tense is its verb?

items.text: Spanish is spoken in twenty-one countries.
Tickets are sold at the door.
The fossil was found by a ten-year-old.
The concert was cancelled because of the storm.
The grades will be posted tomorrow.
Dinner will be served at six.
Someone’s sandwich has been eaten!
The team captains have been chosen.
By noon, the doors had been locked.
The swings were repaired last week.

title: Participle patrol
instructions: Five passive verbs in this school notice use the wrong verb form. Tap each wrong word, then type the past participle.
text: Attention, students! This week the old library was took apart, and the new shelves were build by a team of volunteers. The new books have been chose by your teachers, and the reading rules were wrote on a big poster. Sadly, one window was broke during the move, but it will be fixed soon.

errors.explanation: take, took, taken: the passive needs the participle, “was taken”.
After “were”, use the past participle: “were built”.

title: Passive in every tense
prompt: Write five sentences about how a big school event (a play, a fair, a sports day) is put together. Each sentence uses the passive in a different tense. The tasks are listed above the writing box: write them in order.
tips: Present: is/are + participle. Past: was/were + participle. Future: will be + participle.
Perfect: has/have/had been + participle. Progressive: is/are/was/were being + participle.
Irregular participles: built, chosen, written, sold, made, taken, given, hung.

sentences.ask: Something that is done every year (present passive).
Something that was done last week (past passive).
Something that is being done right now (progressive passive).
Something that has already been done (perfect passive).
Something that will be done on the big day (future passive).

title: Flip it to passive
instructions: Rewrite each active sentence in the passive voice. The receiver goes first, then be + the past participle, then “by” + the doer. Keep the tense.

answers: The bike was fixed by Sam.
items.explanation: Receiver (the bike) + was + fixed + by Sam. Past active → past passive.

answers: The soup is made by the chef.
items.explanation: “Makes” (present) → “is made” (present passive).

items.source: The principal will announce the winners.
answers: The winners will be announced by the principal.
items.explanation: “Will announce” → “will be announced”.

items.source: The crew is painting the stage.
answers: The stage is being painted by the crew.
items.explanation: “Is painting” → “is being painted”.

items.task: Make it passive, and leave out the doer.
hints: “Someone” tells us nothing, so drop it.
items.explanation: “Has eaten” → “has been eaten”. When the doer is unknown, the passive can leave it out.

items.task: Make it passive. Watch the pronoun!
answers: The poem was written by her.
hints: After “by”, use an object pronoun: me, him, her, us, them.
items.explanation: “She” becomes “her” after “by”: “by her”, never “by she”.

title: Flip it to active
instructions: Rewrite each passive sentence in the active voice. Keep the tense, and make the verb agree with its new subject.

items.task: Make it active. Watch the pronoun!
items.source: The trophy was won by them.
hints: “Them” becomes a subject pronoun at the front.
items.explanation: At the front of the sentence, “them” becomes “they”: They won the trophy.

items.source: The cake has been decorated by Lily.
items.explanation: “Has been decorated” → “has decorated”.

items.source: The car is being washed by my brothers.
answers: My brothers are washing the car.
items.explanation: “Is being washed” → “are washing”. The verb now agrees with “my brothers” (plural).

items.source: The results will be posted by Ms. Ruiz.
answers: Ms. Ruiz will post the results.
items.explanation: “Will be posted” → “will post”.

items.source: The roof was damaged by the storm.
items.explanation: “Was damaged” (past passive) → “damaged” (past active).

questions.prompt: Which is the passive of “The dog dug a hole”?

options.text: A hole was dug by the dog.
A hole was digged by the dog.

questions.explanation: dig, dug, dug: “was dug”. “Digged” isn’t a word.

questions.prompt: Which is correct?

options.text: The prize was given to Ana by he.
The prize was given to Ana by him.

questions.explanation: After “by”, use an object pronoun: him, her, them, us, me.

questions.prompt: Which keeps the tense of “The class is planting trees”?

options.text: Trees were planted by the class.
Trees are being planted by the class.
Trees will be planted by the class.

questions.explanation: “Is planting” is present progressive, so the passive is “are being planted” (trees: plural).

questions.prompt: Which is the active of “The muffins were baked by Dad”?
questions.explanation: The doer (Dad) moves to the front, and “were baked” becomes “baked”.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb: “The cookies ___ by the twins.”
questions.explanation: In the passive, the verb agrees with the new subject (cookies, plural): were. And the participle is eaten.

title: Both ways
prompt: Write six sentences about a neighbourhood or school event (a clean-up, a bake sale, a talent show). Write each idea twice, once active and once passive, by following the tasks above the writing box in order.
tips: Active → passive: the receiver moves to the front, add be + participle, and “by” + the doer.
Passive → active: the doer after “by” moves to the front. Keep the tense.
After “by”, use me, him, her, us, them.

sentences.ask: Say what someone did (active, past tense).
Now write sentence 1 in the passive, with “by”.
Say what someone will do (active, with “will”).
Now write sentence 3 in the passive, with “by”.
Something that has been done, without saying who (perfect passive).
Now write sentence 5 in the active, and say who did it.

title: Keep it or flip it?
instructions: Every sentence is passive. Sort it: does the passive work here (the doer is unknown, unimportant or obvious), or would the active be better (the doer is named and matters)?

items.text: My bike was stolen.
The pyramids were built over 4,500 years ago.
The water is heated to 100 °C.
The ball was kicked by Ella into the top corner.
A funny speech was given by our principal.
The winners will be announced on Friday.
The whole pie was eaten by my brother.
Penicillin was discovered in 1928.
The cat was chased by the dog all over the yard.
The cake was baked by me.

questions.prompt: Why is the passive a good choice in “My wallet was stolen”?

options.text: We don’t know who stole it.
It is shorter than the active.

questions.explanation: When the doer is unknown, the passive lets you focus on what happened.

questions.prompt: In a science report, why might you write “The seeds were planted in three pots”?

options.text: The steps matter more than who did them.
It is in the future tense.

questions.explanation: In procedures and reports, the action is the focus, so the passive is common.

questions.prompt: A company says, “Mistakes were made.” What does the passive do here?

options.text: It hides who made the mistakes.
It names who is to blame.

questions.explanation: The passive can dodge responsibility. As a reader, notice it; as a writer, be honest about who did what.

questions.prompt: Which sentence should be flipped to active?

options.text: The winning basket was scored by Ty with one second left.
Rice is grown in many countries.

questions.explanation: Ty is the hero of this sentence, so put him first: “Ty scored the winning basket with one second left.”

questions.prompt: Which is the best reason to choose the passive in an essay?

options.text: To make every sentence sound formal
To keep the focus on the thing the action happens to

questions.explanation: “The Great Wall was built over centuries” keeps the focus on the wall. Use the passive for focus, not to sound fancy.

title: Lab report passives
instructions: This lab report uses the passive because the steps matter more than who did them. Tap the five past participles in its passive verbs.
text: First, the water was poured into a glass beaker. Next, it was heated over a small flame. The temperature was checked every minute, and the bubbles were counted. Finally, the results were recorded in a table.
explanation: was poured · was heated · was checked · were counted · were recorded. Nobody needs to know who held the beaker: the method is what matters.

title: How it’s made
prompt: Explain how something is made or done (pizza, maple syrup, recycling, a school yearbook, a hip-hop track). Write 6–10 sentences. Use the passive at least twice where the doer doesn’t matter, and the active voice at least twice where the doer does matter.
tips: Passive for the process: “The dough is stretched by hand. Then it is topped with sauce.”
Active when the doer matters: “Our neighbour, Mr. Diaz, runs the oven like a pro.”
If you write “by” + a person who matters, try flipping that sentence to active.

title: Active & Passive Voice check
instructions: Ten questions on everything in this unit. You need 8 or more right (80%) to pass. If you don’t pass, you’ll see what to review and get new questions to try again.

questions.prompt: Who is the doer in “The fence was painted by Grandpa”?
questions.explanation: “By Grandpa” names the doer; the fence receives the action.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is passive?

options.text: The children laughed at the clown.
The clown was laughed at by the children.

questions.explanation: “Was laughed at” is be + participle, and the receiver comes first. “Was funny” is a linking verb + adjective.

questions.prompt: What is the receiver in “Lightning struck the old barn”?
questions.explanation: The barn receives the action; lightning does it.

questions.prompt: Is “We were exhausted after the hike” passive?

options.text: No: “exhausted” describes how we felt; nobody did anything to us.

questions.explanation: Feeling words (tired, excited, exhausted) after be work like adjectives. Ask: is there a doer?

questions.prompt: Which sentence is active?

options.text: The goal was blocked by the goalie.

questions.explanation: The doer (the goalie) comes first, before the verb.

questions.prompt: Which is the active version of “The song was written by Mia”?
questions.explanation: Doer (Mia) + verb (wrote) + receiver (the song).

questions.prompt: Why is the active usually stronger in essays?

options.text: It shows who does what, directly and in fewer words.
It is the only correct voice.

questions.explanation: The active is clearer and tighter; the passive is for when the doer doesn’t matter.

questions.prompt: Is “The dog is chasing its tail” active or passive?
questions.explanation: “Is chasing” is be + an -ing verb (progressive). The dog is the doer, so it’s active.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: “The house ___ in 1920.”
questions.explanation: The passive needs the past participle: built.

questions.prompt: Which is the future passive?
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Which is the perfect passive?
questions.explanation: Perfect passive: has/have/had been + past participle.

questions.prompt: Fix it: “The window was broke during the game.”
questions.explanation: break, broke, broken: the passive uses broken.

questions.prompt: Which is the progressive passive?
questions.explanation: Progressive passive: is/are/was/were being + past participle.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb: “The flowers ___ every morning.”
questions.explanation: Flowers is plural → are; and the participle is watered.

questions.prompt: Make it passive: “The coach chose Ana.”

options.text: Ana was chose by the coach.
Ana was chosen by the coach.

questions.explanation: choose, chose, chosen: “was chosen by the coach”.

questions.prompt: Make it passive: “They will open the pool on Monday.”

options.text: The pool will be opened on Monday.
The pool was opened on Monday.
The pool will open them on Monday.

questions.explanation: “Will open” → “will be opened”. “They” tells us nothing, so it can be left out.

questions.prompt: Which is correct?

options.text: The mural was designed by we.
The mural was designed by us.

questions.explanation: After “by”, use an object pronoun: us.

questions.prompt: Make it active: “The pizza is being delivered by Raj.”
questions.explanation: Keep the tense: “is being delivered” (present progressive) → “is delivering”.

questions.prompt: Make it active: “The prize was won by them.”
questions.explanation: At the front, the pronoun is a subject: they.

questions.prompt: Why does the passive work in “The Great Wall was built over many centuries”?

options.text: The builders are many and unknown; the wall is the focus.
The passive is always more formal.
It hides who is to blame.

questions.explanation: When the doer is unknown or unimportant, the passive keeps the focus on the thing.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would be better in the active voice?

options.text: The final speech was delivered by our class president, Zoe.

questions.explanation: Zoe matters in this sentence, so start with her: “Our class president, Zoe, delivered the final speech.”

questions.prompt: What does “Mistakes were made” leave out?
questions.explanation: The passive can hide the doer. Good readers notice when that happens.

questions.prompt: In a science procedure, which sentence fits best?

options.text: The soil was measured with a ruler.
My lab partner Kenji, who is really tall, measured the soil.

questions.explanation: In a procedure, the step matters, not who did it, so the passive fits.

questions.prompt: A paragraph has eight sentences, and seven are passive with “by”. What should the writer do?

options.text: Nothing: the passive is more formal.
Flip most of them to active, keeping the passive only where the doer doesn’t matter.

questions.explanation: Too many passives make writing slow and vague. Choose the passive on purpose.

title: Unit check: breaking news
prompt: Write a news report (at least 6 sentences) about an event at your school or in your town: a flood, a science fair, a record-breaking bake sale, a lost-and-found mystery. Show off this unit: mostly active sentences with the doer first, plus at least two passive sentences used on purpose (the doer is unknown or unimportant), one of them in a tense other than the simple past.
tips: Checklist: doer-first active sentences · two passives on purpose · a passive in the present, future, perfect or progressive.
Passive = be + past participle: was found, will be repaired, has been cancelled.
Named the doer with “by”? Ask yourself if the sentence would be stronger flipped to active.
